the calcite cement in poikiotopic dolostones of the Upper Devonian of New York is postdolomite, that it is a primary cement in some samples, and that it is a secondary cement in other samples.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dolostones were formed in a shallow marine environment with an open marine connection, and that the dolostone formation was controlled by the local and regional hydrology, which in turn was influenced by the tectonics of the area.
poikilotopic textures in dolostones are the product of dolomitization, compaction, and postdolomite cementation, with a possible contribution of dissolution and/or recrystallization.
dolomite is the most important diagenetic agent in poikilotpic dolostones and that dolomitization is a major cause of porosity loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dolomite cementation and dolomitization both occur, but dolomite cementation occurs more frequently.
porosity in the dolostones was reduced by compaction and cementation, but was increased by dolomitization, and that porosity is still being modified by calcite cementation and dissolution.
the porosity of poikilotopic rocks is a function of the relative timing of dolomitization and cementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the porosity of poikilotopic rocks can be very high, but it is very heterogeneous and the porosity distribution is strongly influenced by the timing of dolomite and calcite cementation relative to the timing of compaction.
the porosity history of poikilotopic carbonates is more complex than previously thought, and that porosity is a function of multiple diagenetic events, not just one.
porosity in poikilotropic dolostones is not static.
